title: The MLRO Role and Accountability
summary: What the MLRO is responsible for, the authority, independence and resources the role needs, and how supervisors judge whether an MLRO is effective.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: What the MLRO is responsible for, the authority, independence and resources the role needs, and how supervisors judge whether an MLRO is effective.
Learning Objectives: Explain the MLRO's statutory and regulatory responsibilities
Assess the MLRO's independence, seniority, resources and access to the board
Identify the expectations supervisors have of MLROs and deputies
Syllabus: The MLRO, nominated officer and deputy roles
FATF Recommendations and the risk-based approach
Independence, authority, resources and access to information
What an effective MLRO looks like to a supervisor
Intended Audience: Money laundering reporting officers, nominated officers and their deputies
Heads of financial crime, sanctions and anti-money laundering compliance
Senior financial crime staff preparing to step into the MLRO role
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of anti-money laundering or financial crime compliance in a regulated firm is expected. Prior MLRO experience is helpful, not mandatory.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
